## Replay evidence (orchestrator, 2026-08-20)

Mirrored `scripts/workflow_lint.py:13280-13296` exactly
(`idx = find("**Pre-split completeness guard")`;
`nxt = find("\n\n**", idx+1)`; `region = text[idx:nxt]`; require
`pre_split_review_guard.py` / `PRE-SPLIT-INCOMPLETE` / `remaining:`)
against the live `09-step-5.md` under three placements:

| Placement | region_len | tokens missing | live-tree test |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. live (no insert) | 1443 | none | PASS |
| B. chosen slot (after Round push hygiene) | 1443 | none | PASS |
| C. "forbidden" slot (before Round push hygiene) | 1443 | none | PASS |

`live == chosen == early` all True — the region is BYTE-IDENTICAL under
every placement considered.

Mechanism of the error: the "one position earlier" slot IS the region's
existing terminator position. The region already ends at the `\n\n`
preceding line 38, so whatever paragraph opens there becomes the
terminator. Inserting the ensure heading there merely REPLACES
`**Round push hygiene.**` as the terminator at the SAME byte offset;
nothing is truncated. The original reasoning conflated "becomes the
terminator" with "truncates the region" — those are only the same thing
if the insert lands strictly INSIDE the region.

## The risk is weaker still (control case, orchestrator addition)

Control D inserted the block strictly INSIDE the region (between the
guard paragraph and the ensemble paragraph). The region DID truncate
(1443 -> 1066 chars) — but all three required tokens SURVIVED and the
test would still PASS, because the tokens live at lines 18-28, inside
the first 1,066 chars.

So the honest statement is stronger than "the chosen slot is safe": the
predicate is insensitive to every placement at or after the guard
paragraph's end. Breaking it would require an insert strictly between
the guard heading (line 14) and the last required token (line 28) —
i.e. inside the guard's own prose block, which no reasonable edit would
do.
